title: Review of c22's wave-pinning no-repair finding: replicates on seeds 5-6 and at dt/2; returning the erased protein to the cell lets the cut crawler re-polarize and crawl again, confirming the protein-window mechanism
summary: Labkit pack of the cut world on seeds 5 and 6 plus the author's branch script for front 30%, front 15%, chem and rear cuts, and dt/2 for front 30% and chem. Every arm reproduces the finding: front cuts end as static uniform-high disks (speed 0.000 vs twin 0.30), chem erase is extinct at t=8.96 (8.87 at dt/2), rear cuts keep crawling at 0.26. New control: a one-line variant that returns the erased protein to the cell's cytosol turns the front-30% cut into a recovery (re-polarized half-moon crawling at 0.27 by t=14-16), while the chem erase still dies. Supported.

observations.finding: cuts/front0.3_s5, s6: static uniform-high disk speed 0.000 vs twin 0.301; cuts/chem0.3_s5, s6 extinct t=8.96; cuts/rear0.3_s5, s6 crawl at 0.26; rerun/seed5/sheet.png shows the same in the labkit run

seeds_run.result: pass: front 30/15% static disk, chem extinct, rear crawls; dt/2 identical

controls_run.finding: cuts/dt2_front0.3_s5 and cuts/dt2_chem_s5 (world dt halved); cuts/keepC_front0.3_s5 and cuts/keepC_chem_s5 (erased protein returned to the cell, world_keepC.py)

verdicts.limitation: Planted crawler, one cut time, deterministic dynamics (two seeds differ only in heading). The protein-kept control shows the failure hinges on the protein removed by the cut, so the negative result is specific to cuts that remove polarity protein; noise sweep not repeated.
